examples/cdk/kinesis-cloudwatch-logs/scr.description: KMS --data-dir: run 1 encrypted under the CDK symmetric key, generated a 32-byte data key and signed a precomputed digest with the CDK RSA_2048 key; run 2 with the same --data-dir saw the same KeyId/ARN for both keys, decrypted both ciphertexts by the run-1 key id, read the same public key, and verified the run-1 signature through KMS by the run-1 key id and ARN and outside KMS.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/author.description: HTTP API JWT, REST Cognito and Lambda policy authorizers: a real user was created in the moto pool and real id/access tokens were minted through the Cognito API; the JWT-protected route received requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims and the Cognito-protected route received requestContext.authorizer.claims; a REST TOKEN authorizer, a REST REQUEST authorizer over a header and a query source, and an HTTP API IAM-policy authorizer ran the real policy function and carried its stringified context to the integration, Allow invoked the method, Deny was 403, the documented Unauthorized error was 401, an invalid policy was 500 and a missing identity source was 401 without invoking; a cached TOKEN and HTTP API decision did not invoke the function again until the run clock passed AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/custom.gap: IAM policy evaluation is a docs/125 true limit; S3 is emulated by s3proxy (no bucket policies and no server-side notification hook; the runner delivers bucket notification configurations from observed object state). examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/custom.description: lambda-role custom handler: the compiled asset runs in nodejs:24 and reads String/SecureString/StringList SSM parameters through Ref and GetAtt, a literal SecretString plus the keyed and bare GenerateSecretString forms through GetSecretValue, and the provisioned Cognito pool/client; the runner's local issuer serves the pool JWKS and discovery document; the S3 object round-trip stays real on s3proxy.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/encryp.gap: KMS is emulated by moto (no HSM, key policies or grants); the encrypt/decrypt round-trip is real.
examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/encryp.description: lambda-role encrypted handler: the compiled asset runs in nodejs:24 and round-trips plaintext through the emulated KMS with match=true.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/index..description: lambda-role baseline handler: the compiled asset serves the basic, tracing and dynamic functions and returns the expected 200 payload from each.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/handlers/policy.description: IAM-policy authorizer function for the REST TOKEN, REST REQUEST and HTTP API authorizers; it counts its own invocations and returns the count in the authorizer context, which is how the row proves a cached policy was reused without invoking the function and was re-evaluated per method (GET /token-other is 403 because the cached policy names only GET /token).

examples/cdk/lambda-role/scripts/data-di.gap: s3proxy's filesystem provider persists objects; bucket policies and server-side event hooks are not served by the store.
examples/cdk/lambda-role/scripts/data-di.description: S3 --data-dir: the custom handler wrote an object through the real S3 SDK in one invoke; a second invoke with the same --data-dir read the object back through the handler, and the s3proxy base directory holds the object file.

examples/cdk/lambda-role/scripts/s3-sse..gap: s3proxy's filesystem store refuses server-side encryption by design; the runner's S3 front records SSE-S3 for a verified header-signed put and forwards every other SSE put unchanged, so the store keeps its answer. SSE-KMS and SSE-C remain refused (the runner cannot honour a key binding or customer key). A DeleteObjects body above the front's 1 MiB record buffer is forwarded unchanged and its SSE-S3 records are left for a later plain PutObject, plain CopyObject, successful CompleteMultipartUpload, DeleteObject or plain DeleteBucket to clear; an aborted multipart upload and a metadata subresource read change nothing. Bucket policies and server-side notification hooks are not served by the store.
examples/cdk/lambda-role/scripts/s3-sse..description: SSE-S3 through the real SDK: the compiled Node handler put an object with x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256 and the PutObject response reported AES256; HeadObject and GetObject through the same handler returned the SSE-S3 header and the stored body. One DeleteObjects request at AWS's maximum shape (999 keys of exactly 1024 bytes plus the short recorded key, about 1.05 MiB, above the front's buffer) was forwarded to s3proxy and deleted the object.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/grants.sh.gap: IAM policy evaluation is a docs/125 true limit in general; the local runner evaluates only the enumerated statement shapes docs/127 W3-D1 defines and fails closed on anything else.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/shared-pl.gap: The two runs share one directory on this host; they are not two deployments, and the session that signs the second call is minted by the first run's STS endpoint rather than by a container-to-container hop (that hop is the co-residence work).
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/shared-pl.description: Shared IAM plane: run A's function assumes a role run B's stack defined, through run A's STS endpoint; run B verifies the session's signature from the shared credential registry and grants the call against its own resource policy and the role's identity policy.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-pinn.description: Declared ports: the HTTP API (index 0) is pinned to base+1 and the REST API (index 1) to base, and both pinned listeners answer real signed calls at their declared ports; the unpinned Function URL keeps base+2.
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-pinn.gap: A pin reserves a slot inside the run's --port-base range; a port outside that range is refused rather than bound.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-unpi.description: Unpinned allocation: without --port, the same app keeps today's counter order exactly (httpv2 base, restv1 base+1, fnurl base+2).
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-unpi.gap: The counter is per run; two co-resident runs use distinct --port-base values, as the fixed per-app port blocks require.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-refu.description: Named port refusals: a collision, a port outside the run's range, an unknown logical id and a pin without --port-base each exit non-zero with a message naming the cause before anything starts.
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/port-refu.gap: These refusals are validated at plan time from the derived surface; a port another process holds is reported by the bind, not by the allocator.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/co-reside.description: Shared CA and per-run host names: two runs (auth.localhost and mcp.localhost) reuse one CA at <shared-dir>/ca, each run's leaf carries its own host and verifies against that CA, and both hosts answer over verified HTTPS.
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/co-reside.gap: The CA is a runner-generated local root; the trust is installed per client (the mounted bundle or the harness context), not in a system store.

examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/co-reside.description: Cross-run co-residence: two apps run in two sessions on one shared Docker network and one shared CA with pinned ports; a function in run A signs with run A's credential and calls run B's AWS_IAM route at https://mcp.localhost:<pinned>, and run B verifies it and resolves run A's role.
examples/cdk/local-iam/scripts/co-reside.gap: IAM policy evaluation is narrow (docs/127 W3-D1): only the enumerated statement shapes are evaluated. The two runs are processes on one host sharing a directory and a bridge, not two deployments.

examples/cdk/local-tls/scripts/cloudfron.description: CloudFront in front of the run's own API over TLS: the distribution declares an https-only custom origin, verifies the run CA against its declared origin domain, forwards the origin Host header, and returns the API's GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and a form POST /auth/token unchanged.

examples/cdk/local-tls/scripts/cloudfron.gap: The identity provider the app redirects to is a local test service signed by the runner CA, not a third-party provider; the local edge is not the CloudFront network (docs/125 real network properties).

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/rule-tar.description: EventBridge Lambda rule target; it writes the received Input object to a real SQS receipt queue.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/s3-consu.gap: s3proxy emulates S3 object storage and has no server-side event hook: the runner observes every object change with ListObjectsV2 and therefore reports an observed create as ObjectCreated:Put and an observed delete as ObjectRemoved:Delete; CloudFront caching and the edge network are not involved.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/s3-consu.description: S3 event notifications: the CDK bucket's Lambda, SQS and SNS configurations delivered the documented s3:TestEvent on configuration; the two ObjectCreated configurations share the incoming/ prefix with non-overlapping suffixes, and a real SDK PUT of incoming/a.json delivered ObjectCreated:Put to the Lambda function only (which wrote a real SQS receipt) while the SNS .csv suffix and the queue's event type filtered it; a real SDK PUT of incoming/b.csv delivered ObjectCreated:Put to the SNS topic only; ignored/a.txt was filtered by every prefix/suffix rule; a real SDK DELETE delivered ObjectRemoved:Delete to the queue; describe reported exact per-destination delivered/filtered counts (lambda 1/3, queue 2/3, topic 2/3).

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/sns-cons.description: SNS consumer handler used by the standard, attribute-filtered and body-filtered Lambda subscriptions; it writes a real SQS receipt with the documented Lambda SNS record.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/sns-publ.gap: moto emulates SNS (no managed delivery infrastructure); IAM policy evaluation is a docs/125 true limit. The topics, the publish call and the runner's fan-out are real.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/sns-publ.description: SQS queue SNS publisher: the standard and FIFO topics are provisioned on moto from the CDK definition; the handler publishes through the real SDK; the inline Lambda subscription receives the documented SNS record (message id, subject, timestamp, UnsubscribeUrl, String attributes); the FIFO topic delivers three ordered messages and collapses two identical content-based publishes to one; the FIFO queue carries MessageGroupId and the explicit or content SHA-256 MessageDeduplicationId.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/sns-scen.gap: moto emulates SNS (no managed delivery infrastructure) and ElasticMQ emulates SQS; IAM policy evaluation is a docs/125 true limit. The publishes, the runner's filter evaluation and every target delivery are real.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/sns-scen.description: SNS fan-out targets: an attribute-scope policy (AND across keys, OR within a key) and a body-scope policy (nested keys) each admit one message and filter two; an SQS raw subscription receives the body and native attributes while the envelope subscription receives the documented JSON notification; a loopback HTTP subscription receives the documented body and x-amz-sns-* headers.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.gap: ElasticMQ emulates SQS; IAM, KMS encryption and AWS-managed scaling are not emulated.
examples/cdk/sqs-queue/handlers/worker.m.description: SQS worker handler: the EventsConsumer mapping batched two real ElasticMQ messages on the 10s window and left only the reported failure; FilteredConsumer deleted a non-matching message without invocation; FifoConsumer kept a failed group's records in order; ConcurrencyConsumer's live peak stayed at MaximumConcurrency=2.

examples/cdk/sqs-queue/scripts/data-dir-.description: SQS --data-dir: a real ElasticMQ message was sent to an unconsumed queue in one session; a second session with the same --data-dir found it visible and received its body; the messages-storage H2 database held it.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.gap: CloudFront edge network (docs/125 true limit); the gateway forwards a streamed response at the origin's pace and caches it in full after it completes (Lambda's 6 MB uncapped burst and 2 MBps streaming cap are not reproduced).
examples/cdk/ssr-site/bin/apptheory-ssr-.description: SSR site: the origin group fails over from the S3 HTML primary (403 under OAC) to the real SSR handler; the SSR stream reaches the viewer through the gateway and directly on the Function URL as the handler writes it, the viewer-response function echoes the request id, and the assets and hydrate deployments, full and ranged HEAD, conditional If-None-Match GETs, OPTIONS and the missing-object 403 are asserted. Caching is real: the static-assets behavior answered a miss then a hit with x-cache and age, the CACHING_DISABLED SSR behavior never cached, an invalidation through the local API and through the aws CLI removed the object, and clock.advance past the TTL was a miss again.

examples/cdk/ssr-site/scripts/upload-ass.gap: The edge network and IAM policy evaluation are docs/125 true limits (real network properties; IAM policy evaluation in general).

The site's bucket declares no event notification; the notification destinations are proven by the sqs-queue row. s3proxy serves the objects without bucket policies or IAM.
